newsitem.title: SPAIN: Repsol signs exploration deal with Trinidad.
newsitem.headline: Repsol signs exploration deal with Trinidad.

text.p: Spanish petrochemical group Repsol said on Tuesday its Tobago unit and Amoco Trinidad Gas had signed a new exploration contract with Trinidad's Energy Ministry.
Repsol said it held a 30 percent interest in the contract, while Amoco had a controlling 70 percent.
The contract opens a 737 square km area to exploration, situated in the waters surrounding Venezuela, some 90 km from Trinidad.
Repsol also said it had a 20 percent interest in Atlantic LNG of Trinidad and Tobago which is constructing a $1 billion liquefied natural gas plant.

The company said the plant would produce three million tonnes of liquefied natural gas a year and that Enagas, a unit of the Natural Gas Group, would purchase 40 percent of the gas produced for sale in Spain.
The remaining 60 percent will be sold to Cabot LNG for the northeastern markets of the United States.
"Repsol's participation in this project consolidates the growing importance that natural gas has within its activities," the company said in a statement.
